prerequisites: Knowledge of the lower layers (physical and data link) of the OSI model, included in the Fundamentals of Telematics course.
Proficiency in binary, decimal, and hexadecimal numerical representations.

learning_outcomes.text: Recognize topologies in local area networks, name potential protocols, and explain their operation.
Analyze, elaborate, and determine relevant information in the development of tasks related to the different topics covered in the subject.
Know network routing and interconnection methods.
Analyze and evaluate routing protocols using software tools.
Create and use models of real networks using network simulators.

syllabus_topics: Topic 1: Review of physical and data link layers
Routing: Classification, strategies and minimum cost algorithms
Introduction to congestion control and traffic management techniques
Interior routing protocols: RIP, introduction to OSPF
Exterior routing protocols: Introduction to BGP
assessment_rules: To pass the course, both theory (Nt) and practical (Np) blocks must be passed with a minimum of 5 out of 10 points. If either block is not passed, the maximum final grade will be 4.5 points. If both blocks are passed, the final grade is calculated as 0.6 * Nt + 0.4 * Np. In the ordinary call, Nt is based on controls (mean of >=4, otherwise max 4.5), potentially a global theory exam. Np requires 80% attendance and is 0.1 * Average Activities + 0.9 * Final Practical Exam. For other calls, Nt and Np are based on respective exams.
